_about: How names and recurring terms are written in this language on Deovandski's site, so they are always spelled the same. Names are written by sound, never translated (the author's rule). #HusbandOutWorld names come from HusbandOutWorld's content/i18n/hi/glossary.json, which is the source: the names below are copied from it for the ones this site uses. Correct a series name there and here together, and look up any other series name there. Add this site's own names here the first time you translate them.
rule: Series names follow HusbandOutWorld's rule for this language: Story names in Devanagari, by sound (हैरी, सनबी, फ़ॉरवे, बुरेज़). This covers coined world terms written as names too: creatures, plants, nari gels, spells, factions, guilds, ranks and coins (Bleed Out = ब्लीड आउट, Red Winga = रेड विंगा, Sapphire = सफ़ायर). Nari is written नरी, not नारी, because नारी means 'woman' in Hindi. A few descriptive place and object names whose plain meaning matters are translated (Nari Stones = नरी पत्थर, Black Honey = काला शहद, Bone Wood = हड्डी-लकड़ी, Blood Book = रक्त-ग्रंथ). The reader is addressed as तुम; sentences end with ।; digits are Western. The currency balls is गेंदें (sing. गेंद; सफ़ायर गेंद); the 'balls' double meaning is lost, so lines about courage use जिगरा. The unit timehunk is टाइमहंक; A.G. and B.G. stay in Latin letters. Real people (Deovandski, Deo, Mitsukiven, Mitsuken, Feiourm), the title and pets named in the afterwords (Peeta) stay in Latin letters. Logogram verb names drawn on the images (Transmute, Entangle, Right, Up...) stay in Latin letters. 'Sanbi shit!' (the Sanbi oath) is always बूढ़ी सनबी आत्मा! ('Old Sanbi soul!'), the author's rule.
site_rules: Real people and pets stay in Latin letters: Deovandski, Deo, and every family member, friend and pet named on the site (Peeta, Bidu, Fluffy).
Brand, company and product names stay as they are (Wizard Deo Solutions, Microsoft, Dynamics 365 F&O, GitHub, LinkedIn).

Titles in the top-39 lists (games, anime, TV, movies), concerts and theater (Deo's answer on #87): use the official title in this language. Movies and TV shows use their official local title; if none exists, keep the English one. Anime keeps the 'Romaji (local title)' structure; in Japanese, show the official Japanese title.
Anything marked translate="no" (Vraki-typeface text, names in a logo, code) stays as it is.
Every tab is translated, Lust, Tattoo and Mentor included (Deo's answer on #87).
